title: SoftHateBench: Evaluating Moderation Models Against Reasoning-Driven, Policy-Compliant Hostility
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the performance of content moderation models (classifiers and LLMs) in detecting 'soft hate speech' targeting religious groups. Soft hate speech is defined as reasoning-driven, policy-compliant hostility that masks explicit toxicity while preserving a hostile standpoint. The study specifically measures the 'Hate Success Rate' (HSR) on generated arguments targeting religious identities (e.g., claiming a group causes harm to community values) compared to explicit 'hard' hate speech.
findings: The study found that while moderation models perform well on explicit 'hard' hate speech against religious groups, their performance drops significantly when the same hostile standpoints are framed as 'soft hate' (e.g., policy-compliant arguments). Specifically, instruction-tuned LLMs showed the highest performance on 'Hard' hate for Religion/Belief but still degraded substantially on soft variants. Encoder-based models nearly collapsed on soft religious hate, failing to detect reasoning-driven hostility lacking explicit toxic keywords.
